svg.text: THE ONE BIT · 7 UNIQUE PROPERTIES · EACH A THEOREM

text.font-family: PNPMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: SAT ∉ P cannot hold without the
transfer, and with the hardness half
cited neither can P ≠ NP. Whatever
proves either proves the bit first.

tspan.font-family: PNPMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace
PNPMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: The bit alone, the one explicit
premise, gives SAT ∉ P in one step
and P ≠ NP with nothing cited.

svg.text: Every so-called other way to P ≠ NP
is our way in different vocabulary: it
delivers both kinds, and if the bit
failed it would fail with it.
